cards.claim: Cubic Newton–Schulz achieves near-identical training quality to quintic Newton–Schulz across diverse settings
cards.conditions: GPT-2 Small; hybrid MoE/Mamba models (1B–4B parameters); using cubic5 (five-step cubic construction) vs Muon-Jordan quintic updates
cards.effect: ~10^−3 validation loss difference; "nearly indistinguishable final loss"
cards.evidence: Empirical training experiments across synthetic diagnostics, NanoGPT ablations, and large-model training
cards.quote: cubic5 matches the Muon-Jordan quintic update within about $10^{-3}$ validation loss on hybrid MoE/Mamba models with one billion to four billion parameters

cards.claim: Training quality is not monotonically governed by polar-decomposition accuracy
cards.conditions: GPT-2 Small; multiple polar-factor variants tested (truncated Polar Express, Muon-Jordan, cubic Newton–Schulz, FP32 SVD)
cards.effect: Different orthogonalization methods reach "nearly indistinguishable" final loss despite varying polar accuracy
cards.evidence: Comparative empirical results across multiple orthogonalization schemes
cards.quote: training quality is not governed monotonically by polar-decomposition accuracy: truncated Polar Express, Muon-Jordan, cubic Newton–Schulz, and an explicit FP32 SVD polar factor can reach nearly indistinguishable final loss on GPT-2 Small

cards.claim: Cubic Newton–Schulz is computationally cheaper than quintic Newton–Schulz (principled low-cost variant)
cards.conditions: Matrix multiplication count comparison across five iterations
cards.effect: 10 dominant matrix multiplications (cubic) vs 15 (quintic); ~33% reduction in FLOP count per orthogonalization step
cards.quote: The resulting five-step cubic construction uses ten dominant matrix multiplications, compared with fifteen for five quintic Newton–Schulz iterations.

cards.claim: Cubic5 is a practical low-cost Muon orthogonalization variant with empirical parity to quintic methods
cards.conditions: Tested on GPT-2 Small and hybrid MoE/Mamba (1B–4B params); cubic schedule derived for Muon's low-precision singular value band
cards.effect: Training-quality parity with quintic, at reduced computational cost
cards.evidence: Synthetic diagnostics, NanoGPT ablations, and large-model experiments
cards.quote: These results support cubic5 as a practical low-cost Muon orthogonalization variant, with empirical evidence of training-quality parity in the settings tested.
